about: The font page's glossary (site/index.html, 6. Glossary), written by the Builder's Glyphs > Glossary.
`groups` are the section titles ("1: Left Hand"; `nav` is the contents' short name for one), each with a
description and its subtitles in page order; `sections` are the subtitles ("1a: Left Hand Finger"), each with a
title, a description, its default example and its rows in page order. Descriptions are a little Markdown:
paragraphs, **bold**, *italic*, `typed examples`, [links](https://…), "- " lists, and the page's <u>, <jzp>, <text>,

and
; any other HTML shows as text. A section title whose subtitles are all hidden isn't on the page either.
`cd builder && python3 -m jzpbuild.glossary` rewrites the glossary between the <!-- glossary all --> markers and the
contents links between <!-- glossary nav --> (a release does it too); the rest of the page stays as written.
A row is a glyph, {"glyph": "lg_gou"}, or a word written together, {"word": "少息", "glyphs": ["md_shao", "md_xi"]};
its ASCII, 中文 and 拼音 come from the glyphs' spellings in builder/inputs/components.csv. "meaning" (optional) fills
the Definition column, which a section gets once one of its rows has one. "typed" (optional) is what was typed to add or edit the row.
Every glyph with spellings is in some section, on its own or in a word; a hidden one leaves it out on purpose.
Columns: ASCII | 中文 | 拼音 | Input | Output | Definition: Output is the row's example and Input how to type it. A subtitle's "usage"
(optional) is its default example as [ASCII, 中文]: {} is the row's glyph's spelling, marked red; <r>…</r> marks more. Without one, each row
is typed on its own, after a colon where the font needs one, and consecutive numbers (md_1 to md_13) share one row. A row's own "usage"
(the Builder's Input column) replaces either; a word is typed on its own unless it has one. (Older files' "kind" said which.)
"hidden": true on a subtitle or a section title (the Builder's eye switch) leaves it off the page; its glyphs count as left out on purpose.

groups.title: 3. Numbers for String and Hui
groups.description: NOTE: You can also use decimals for hui numbers

groups.title: 4. Other
groups.description: These are used in vertical layouts. Option to preface with `:` to write the character by itself. Best use Chinese characters to avoid ambiguity with homonym pinyins.

1b.title: 1.2. Speed
1b.description: The characters affect the 韵 (yùn) or rhythm

rows.meaning: hit the string with force with thumb, bam!
pluck with left thumb inward while holding down hui
lightly tap instead of pressing down, plays a harmonic
pluck inwards with left hand (usually ring finger)
push out to pluck with left hand (usually middle finger)

2b.title: 2.2. Chords and Multi-Note
2b.description:
These notes are written with strings noted on the right and left. Preface the character with the chord key, and then separate the right v. left with a `|`.

ex: `Cs9,3|05` or `撮名九,三｜散五` will make <jzp>Cs9,3|05</jzp>

2c.title: 2.3. Other Right Hand Techniques
2c.description:
<u>For use in Vertical Layout only</u>
<small>preface these with `:` and best use Chinese characters to avoid ambiguity with homonym pinyins</small>

rows.meaning: pluck a string with the ring, middle and index finger out in quick succession
pluck a string with the ring, middle out in quick succession
short pause, like a little sigh
If there's a character that isn't part of the font, this is just a placeholder
